title: Thursday Quick Tip
subtitle: When a kid drifts
hook: One kid is picking grass in right field.
intro: You are halfway through the instructions.
One player is drawing in the dirt with a cleat.
statement: Kids drift when they are waiting, not when they are moving.
q1: Do you call the player back in by name —
q2: or shorten the talk and get everyone moving?
t1: There is no perfect answer here. But attention comes back
t2: when kids have something to do.
cta: Coaches — what do you do when a kid drifts?
ctaLines: Say their name. Hand them the ball. Start the drill.
Redirect the kid or change the pace?
ctaPrompt: Share your attention habit below. There are no wrong answers.
caption:
One kid is picking grass in right field.
You are halfway through the instructions. One player is drawing in the dirt with a cleat.
Kids drift when they are waiting, not when they are moving.
Call them back or get everyone moving. There is no perfect answer.
What do you do when a kid drifts? Share your habit in the comments.
